description: Maya keeps a first-edition novel that belonged to her grandmother and is organizing an informal family reading afternoon. She must make the final call about the time, reading format, handling of the book, and which passage the family will feature.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Heirloom Book Keeper and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family has an informal afternoon planned around reading from Maya's first-edition copy of their grandmother's favorite novel.
shared_context.S2: Maya is keeping the book and will make the final decision about the gathering plan.
shared_context.S3: The house has a living room with seating and a reading lamp, and the original book is currently kept there.
shared_context.S4: Maya's usual family-planning habit is to ask each person in turn for anything that should shape the plan before she settles it.

PF1.text: Rosa has low vision and needs a projected 20-point large-print companion text to follow the reading; she can attend only on 2027-04-11 from 15:00 to 16:00.

PF2.text: Jonah asked a rare-book conservator for advice, and the conservator recommended displaying the original in a book cradle without letting anyone handle it; Jonah has not shared that advice with the group yet.

PF3.text: Leah found a note in their grandmother's recipe box saying that chapter 7 of the novel should be the family reading's featured passage; she has not shown the note to the group yet.

acceptance_conditions: The reading must be scheduled for 2027-04-11 from 15:00 to 16:00.
A projected 20-point large-print companion text must be provided.
The original must be displayed in a book cradle and not handled by guests.
Chapter 7 must be the featured passage.
The settlement must include a commitment to prepare and project the 20-point companion text.
Jonah's conservator advice must be cited as justification after Jonah reveals it.

content_checks.C1: 'April 11' in decisions['reading_datetime'] and '2027' in decisions['reading_datetime'] and '3:00' in decisions['reading_datetime'] and '4:00' in decisions['reading_datetime']
content_checks.C2: 'projected' in decisions['reading_format'] and '20-point' in decisions['reading_format'] and 'large-print companion text' in decisions['reading_format']
content_checks.C3: 'book cradle' in decisions['book_handling'] and ('not handled' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'without' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'no one' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'no guest' in decisions['book_handling'])
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] in ['accommodation', 'accessibility', 'logistics'] and c['target'] == 'Rosa' and 'projected' in c['detail'] and '20-point' in c['detail'] and 'large-print companion text' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and any(r['fact_id'] == 'PF2' and r['speaker'] == 'A3' for r in revealed) and 'book cradle' in decisions['book_handling'] and ('not handled' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'without' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'no one' in decisions['book_handling'] or 'no guest' in decisions['book_handling'])

decisive_facts.why: Rosa's availability changes the gathering time to exactly 2027-04-11 15:00-16:00, and her low vision changes the reading format to a projected 20-point companion text and requires its preparation commitment.
The conservator's advice changes book handling from ordinary guest reading to display in a book cradle with no guest handling, and it supplies the fact that must be cited after Jonah speaks.
The grandmother's note changes the featured passage from an arbitrary selection to exactly chapter 7.
